"Would that you had asked the hosts of Kindah, on the day they turned back, where is which of us?"

And another said:

"How many a blessing was his, how many, how many."

The Qur'an was revealed in the language of the Arabs, and they repeat a thing for its emphasis.

Fourth: Its meaning is: "That is ten complete in the distinction (*fasl*), even though the three are during Hajj and the seven are after it, so that it does not come to anyone's mind that the seven are less than the three." This was said by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

Fifth: It is a statement in the form of a report, but its meaning is an imperative. Its implied meaning is: "That is ten, so complete them."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This is for whoever's family is not present at the Sacred Mosque﴾. Regarding what is referred to by "this," there are two sayings: The first: it is the enjoyment (*tamattu'*) by Umrah until Hajj. The second: it is the recompense by the sacrifice and the fasting. The *lam* in "for whoever" in this view carries the meaning of "upon." As for "those present at the Sacred Mosque": Ibn Abbas, Tawus, and Mujahid said: They are the people of the Sacred Precinct (*al-haram*). Ata' said: They are whoever's dwelling is within the *mawaqit* (the stations of ihram). Ibn al-Anbari said: The meaning of the verse is that this obligation is for those who are from outside, and He only mentioned "his family" (*ahluh*), which is what is meant by "presence," because the usual thing for a man is that he resides where his family resides.

**The Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 2, Verse 197**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The Hajj (the major pilgrimage) is in well-known months﴾

There are two dialectal forms of the word *al-Hajj*. Opening the *ḥā'* (*ḥajj*) is the form of the people of the Hijaz, and most readers recited it that way. Pronouncing it with a *kasrah* (*ḥijj*) is the form of Tamim, and it is said to be the form of the people of Najd. Al-Hasan recited it that way. Sibawayh said: one says *ḥajja ḥajjan*, like their saying *dhakara dhikran* (he mentioned). They also say *ḥijjah*, meaning he performed the Hajj for one year. Al-Farra' said: the meaning is that at the time of the Hajj these are the months. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that the months of the Hajj are well-known months.

Regarding the months of the Hajj, there are two views. The first is that they are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Ata', al-Sha'bi, Tawus, al-Nakha'i, Qatadah, Makhul, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Abu Hanifah, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with them all. The second is that they are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah in full. This is also narrated from Ibn Umar, and from Ata', Tawus, Mujahid, al-Zuhri, al-Rabi', and Malik ibn Anas. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: these scholars only meant that these months are not the months of the lesser pilgrimage ('Umrah); they are for the Hajj, even though the rites of the Hajj end with the conclusion of Mina. They used to prefer performing 'Umrah outside of them. Ibn Sirin said: no one of the people of knowledge doubts that 'Umrah outside the months of the Hajj is more excellent than 'Umrah within the months of the Hajj. He said ﴿The Hajj is in months﴾ although they are two months and part of a third, following the custom of the Arabs. Al-Farra' said: the Arabs say, "For him there are two days, I have not seen him," when it is only one day and part of another. They also say, "I visited you this year" and "I came to you today," when the action occurred within a single hour. Ibn al-Anbari mentioned two explanations for this. The first is that the Arabs use the plural to refer to the dual, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those are free of what they say﴾, where He means 'A'ishah and Safwan. Likewise His saying: ﴿And We were witnesses to their judgment﴾, where He means Dawud and Sulayman. The second is that the Arabs attribute a long period of time to a short period of time, so they say, "Ibn al-Zubayr was killed during the days of the Hajj," although the killing occurred in a very short time.

**Section**

The scholars differed concerning one who entered the state of ihram for the Hajj before the months of the Hajj. Ata', Tawus, Mujahid, and al-Shafi'i said: this is not valid for him. They took the purpose of His saying ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months﴾ to be that the Hajj is not validly concluded except within them. Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Thawri, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: entering ihram for the Hajj before the months is valid. According to this view, His saying ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months﴾ means that most of the Hajj takes place in these months, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Hajj is 'Arafah."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever undertakes the Hajj therein﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: it means the declaration of the Hajj (*al-ihlal*) and entering into ihram for it. Tawus and Ata' said: it means that he recites the talbiyah (the pilgrim's chant). It is narrated from Ali, Ibn Umar, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, and others that if one garlands his sacrificial animal (*hady*) he has entered ihram. This is understood to mean that he garlanded it intending the Hajj. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him, stated in the narration of al-Athram that ihram is by intention. It was asked of him: could one be in ihram without the talbiyah? He said: yes, if he resolves to enter ihram. This is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i. Abu Hanifah said: entering ihram is not permitted except by the talbiyah or by garlanding and driving the sacrificial animal.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There shall be no obscenity (*rafath*)﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Abu Ja'far recited: "*fa-la rafatha wa la fusuqa*" with a *ḍammah* and tanwin. Nafi', Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i recited it without tanwin, and none of them put a *ḍammah* on the *lām* of *jidal* except Abu Ja'far. Abu Ali said: the argument of the one who opened (the final vowel) is that it is more precisely suited to the intended meaning, because by using the *fatḥah* he negated all of obscenity and wrongdoing, like His saying ﴿There is no doubt in it﴾. When he uses *ḍammah* with tanwin, the negation applies to one instance of it. They used *fatḥah* on the *lām* of *jidal* so that the negation would encompass its entire category. Likewise the two nouns before it should be read together. The argument of the one who used *ḍammah* is that the negation of all obscenity is understood from the context of the speech, and the wording may be singular while the intended meaning is the whole.

Regarding *al-rafath* (obscenity) there are three views. The first is that it is sexual intercourse, said by Ibn Umar, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others. The second is that it is sexual intercourse and whatever falls short of it, such as allusion to it. This is also narrated from Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Amr ibn Dinar, among others. The third is that it is idle speech, said by Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Yazidi. Regarding *al-fusuq* (wrongdoing) there are three views. The first is that it is cursing, said by Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Ibrahim, and others. The second is calling one another by offensive nicknames, such as saying to your brother, "O wicked one! O wrongdoer!" This was narrated by al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. The third is that it is acts of disobedience, said by al-Hasan, Ata', Tawus, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others. This is the view we choose, because acts of disobedience include all of these, and because the *fasiq* is one who goes out of obedience into disobedience.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nor disputation (*jidal*) in the Hajj﴾. *Al-jidal* is contention (*al-mira'*). There are two views regarding the meaning of the statement.

The first is that its meaning is: let no one argue with another, lest the argument lead him to anger and to doing what is unbefitting the Hajj. Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Tawus, Ata', Ikrimah, al-Nakha'i, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, al-Dahhak, and others held this view.

The second is that its meaning is: there is no doubt and no dispute about the Hajj, for its matter has been settled, its time is known, and the intercalation (*al-nasi'*) has been removed from it. Mujahid said: they used to perform the Hajj in Dhu al-Hijjah for two years, then in Muharram for two years, then in Safar for two years, and they would perform the Hajj in every month for two years, until the Hajj of Abu Bakr coincided with the second of the two years in Dhu al-Qa'dah, one year before the Hajj of the Prophet (ﷺ). Then the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Hajj in Dhu al-Hijjah, which is the year in which he said: "Indeed, time has returned to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth." This view was held by al-Suddi, from his teachers, and by al-Qasim ibn Muhammad.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety﴾. Ibn Abbas said: the people of Yemen used to perform the Hajj without taking provisions, saying, "We are those who rely upon Allah," and so they would beg from the people. Then Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: they were commanded to take provisions, and they were informed that the best of what they take as provision is the piety of Allah, mighty and majestic.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 198–199:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They used to avoid trade and buying and selling during the season (al-mawsim), and they would say: "These are days of remembrance (dhikr)." So this verse was revealed. Al-ibtigha' (seeking) means al-iltimas (pursuit, seeking). The fadl (bounty) here means seeking sustenance through trade and earning. Ibn Qutayba said: afadtum means dafaʿtum (you pressed on, you surged forth). Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that you surged forth in large numbers; it is said: "Afada al-qawm fi al-hadith" when they rushed into it and engaged in it extensively.

Regarding the naming of ʿArafat there are two opinions.

(p-213) The first: that Allah, exalted is He, sent Jibril to Ibrahim and he performed the hajj with him; when he reached ʿArafat he said: "I have recognized (ʿaraftu)," so it was named ʿArafa. This was said by ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him.

The second: that it was named thus because Adam and Hawwa' gathered there and recognized one another (taʿarrufihima). This was said by al-Dahhak.

Al-Zajjaj said: al-mashʿar is the landmark, named so because prayer is performed at it. Standing, spending the night, and supplication are among the landmarks of the Hajj, and it is Muzdalifa, which is a single gathering place known by both names. Ibn ʿUmar and Mujahid said: al-Mashʿar al-Haram is all of Muzdalifa.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember Him as He has guided you﴾, meaning: in recompense for His guidance to you. If it is asked: what is the benefit of repeating the remembrance? It is answered: there are four responses. The first: He repeated it for emphasis in commanding it. The second: the second remembrance is connected to something the first was not connected to, so its repetition is fine; the meaning is: remember Him by His oneness as He reminded you by His guidance. The third: He repeated it to indicate its continuity; the meaning is: remember Him with remembrance after remembrance. Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahwi mentioned these sayings. The fourth: the remembrance in His saying ﴿remember Allah at the sacred landmark﴾ is the prayer of Maghrib and ʿIsha, which are combined at Muzdalifa, and the remembrance in His saying ﴿as He has guided you﴾ is the remembrance performed at the standing at Muzdalifa on the morning of the gathering (ghadat jamʿ). This was related by al-Qadi Abu Yaʿla.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, before it, you were among those astray﴾. Regarding the pronoun (haʾ al-kinaya) there are three opinions. The first: it refers to Islam; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas. The second: it refers to guidance; this was said by Muqatil and al-Zajjaj. The third: it refers to the Qur'an; this was said by Sufyan al-Thawri.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then depart from where the people depart﴾. ʿA'isha said: Quraysh and those who followed their religion, who were the Hums, used to stand at ʿArafat... they would stand in the evening of ʿArafa at Muzdalifa, saying: "We are the people of the House (qataN al-bayt)," while the rest of the Arabs and people would stand at ʿArafat, so this verse was revealed. Al-Zajjaj said: they were called al-Hums because they were zealous (tahammasu) in their religion, meaning they were strict; al-hamasa is severity in everything.

Regarding the referent of "the people" (al-nas) here there are four opinions. The first: they are all the Arabs other than the Hums, and this is supported by the hadith of ʿA'isha; this is the view of ʿUrwa, Mujahid, and Qatada. The second: the intended "people" here is Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him; this was said by al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim. The third: the intended "people" is Adam; this was said by al-Zuhri. Abu al-Mutawakkil, Abu Nahik, and Muriq al-Ijli recited "al-nasi" with the yaʾ affirmed. The fourth: they are the people of Yemen and Rabiʿa, for they used to depart from ʿArafat; this was said by Muqatil.

Regarding those addressed by this there are two opinions. One: it is addressed to Quraysh, and this is the view of the majority. The second: it is addressed to all Muslims, and this follows the view of those who say "the people" means Adam or Ibrahim. The departure (ifada) here, according to the apparent meaning of the wording, is the departure from Muzdalifa to Mina on the morning of the sacrifice; however, the majority of the exegetes hold that it is departure from ʿArafat, so the apparent meaning of the speech does not require that. How can it be said: ﴿When you depart from ʿArafat, remember Allah﴾, then ﴿depart from ʿArafat﴾? Nevertheless, I say: the construction of the speech, as the people of tafsir have said, involves inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir); its intended sense is: ﴿Then depart from where the people depart﴾, and when you depart from ʿArafat, remember Allah.

"Al-Ghafur" is one of the names of Allah, mighty and majestic. It derives from your saying: "ghafartu al-shay'" when I covered it, so al-Ghafur is the one who covers His servant with His mercy, or who covers the sins of His servants. Al-Ghafur is the one who grants forgiveness abundantly, since the form fa'ul is for intensification in quantity, as in your saying: sabur, darub, and akul.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 200–203:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when you have completed your rites (manasik), remember Allah﴾

Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are three opinions.

The first: The people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam), when they gathered at the season (al-mawsim), would recount the deeds of their fathers, their days (battles) and their lineages in the Jahiliyyah, and they would boast of that; so this verse was revealed. This meaning is related from al-Hasan, ʿAtaʾ and Mujahid.

The second: The Arabs, when they related something or spoke, would say: "By your father, they did such and such," so this verse was revealed. This is also related from al-Hasan.

The third: When they had completed their rites, a man would stand at Mina and say: "O Allah, my father was great in generosity (ʿazim al-jafnah), abundant in wealth, so give me the like of that." He would not mention Allah; he mentions only his father, and asks to be given in his worldly life. So this verse was revealed. This is the saying of al-Suddi.

Al-manasik: the acts of worship (al-mutaʿabbadat). Regarding what is meant here there are two opinions. The first: it is all the acts of the Hajj, as said by al-Hasan. The second: it is the shedding of blood (sacrifice), as said by Mujahid.

Regarding their mention of their fathers there are four opinions. The first: it is their acknowledgment of them. The second: it is their swearing by them. The third: it is their mention of their fathers' kindness toward them, for they would remember their fathers and forget Allah's kindness toward them. The fourth: it is the remembrance by children of their fathers, because it is the first thing they utter; this meaning is related from ʿAtaʾ and al-Dahhak.

Regarding "aw" (or) there are two opinions. The first: it means "bal" (rather). The second: it means "wa" (and). And "al-khalaq" (portion) has already been mentioned.

Regarding the "good in this world" (hasanat al-dunya) there are seven opinions. The first: it is the righteous wife, as said by ʿAli. The second: it is worship, related by Sufyan ibn Husayn from al-Hasan. The third: it is knowledge and worship, related by Hisham from al-Hasan. The fourth: it is wealth, as said by Abu Wail, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. The fifth: it is well-being (ʿafiyah), as said by Qatadah. The sixth: it is abundant provision (al-rizq al-wasiʿ), as said by Muqatil. The seventh: it is blessing (niʿmah), as said by Ibn Qutaybah.

Regarding the "good in the Hereafter" there are three opinions. The first: it is the wide-eyed maidens (al-hur al-ʿin), as said by ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him. The second: it is Paradise, as said by al-Hasan, al-Suddi and Muqatil. The third: it is pardon and well-being, related from al-Hasan and al-Thawri.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They shall have a share of what they have earned﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that their supplication is answered, because their earning here is the supplication. This verse is connected to what precedes it, except that it has been related that it was revealed upon an occasion different from that of its companions. al-Dahhak related from Ibn ʿAbbas that "a man said: O Messenger of Allah, my father died without performing Hajj; may I perform Hajj on his behalf? He said: 'If your father had a debt and you paid it, would that not have discharged it for him?' He said: Yes. He said: 'The debt of Allah is more deserving to be paid!' He said: Then do I have a reward? So this verse was revealed."

Regarding the meaning of "swiftness of reckoning" there are five opinions. The first: it is its scarcity (qillatuh), as said by Ibn ʿAbbas. The second: it is its nearness of coming, said by Muqatil. The third: that when He knows what is for the one being reckoned and what is against him before his reckoning, He is swift in reckoning him for that. The fourth: the meaning is: and Allah is swift in recompense; al-Zajjaj mentioned this opinion and the one before it. The fifth: that He has no need of thought and deliberation as the incapable do, said by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And remember Allah during appointed days﴾. Regarding this remembrance there are two opinions. The first: it is the takbir at the jamarat (pillars), after the prescribed prayers, and at other times of the Hajj. The second: it is the takbir following the obligatory prayers. The proponents of this second view differed regarding the time at which the takbir begins and ends, in six opinions. The first: one says takbir from the Fajr prayer on the Day of ʿArafah until after the ʿAsr prayer on the last day of al-tashriq; this is said by ʿAli, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad. The second: from the Fajr prayer on the Day of ʿArafah until the ʿAsr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice (al-nahr); this is said by Ibn Masʿud and Abu Hanifah. The third: from after the Zuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until after the ʿAsr prayer on the last day of al-tashriq; this is said by Ibn ʿUmar, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAtaʾ. The fourth: one says takbir from the Zuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until after the Zuhr prayer on the day of departure (al-nafar), which is the second day of al-tashriq; this is said by al-Hasan. The fifth: one says takbir from Zuhr on the Day of Sacrifice until the Subh prayer on the last day of al-tashriq; this is said by Malik ibn Anas, and it is one of the two opinions of al-Shafiʿi. The sixth: one says takbir from the Maghrib prayer on the night of Sacrifice until the Subh prayer on the last day of al-tashriq; this is a view of al-Shafiʿi. The school of our imam Ahmad holds that when one is not in ihram, he says takbir after twenty-three prayers, the first being Fajr on the Day of ʿArafah and the last being ʿAsr on the last day of al-tashriq; and when one is in ihram, he says takbir after seventeen prayers, the first being Zuhr on the Day of Sacrifice and the last being ʿAsr on the last day of al-tashriq.

Is this takbir after the obligatory prayers restricted to their being performed in congregation or not? On this there are two narrations from Ahmad. The first: it is restricted to one who prays in congregation; this is the view of Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him. The second: it is restricted to the obligatory prayer, even if one prays it alone; this is the view of al-Shafiʿi.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the worldly life impresses you﴾.

They differed as to who this verse was revealed concerning, in three views. The first is that it was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who had smooth speech and a disbelieving heart. He would show the Prophet good will, swear to him that he loved him, and follow him in his religion while concealing otherwise. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi and Muqatil. The second is that it was revealed concerning one who was a hypocrite, who expressed with his tongue what was not in his heart. This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd. The third is that it was revealed concerning the expedition of al-Raji' (sariyyat al-Raji', a small military detachment), and that "the disbelievers of Quraysh sent to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in Medina: 'We have embraced Islam, so send us some men of your companions to teach us our religion.' The Prophet ﷺ sent Khubayb ibn Adi, Murthad al-Ghanawi, Khalid ibn Bukayr, Abdullah ibn Tariq and Zayd ibn al-Dithnah, and appointed Asim ibn Thabit over them. They set out toward Mecca and stopped between Mecca and Medina, and they had dates with them, so they ate from them. An old woman passed by, saw the date pits, and returned to her people saying: 'The people of Yathrib have taken this route.' Seventy men of them mounted and surrounded them, and fought them, and they killed Murthad, Khalid and Ibn Tariq. Asim emptied his quiver, which contained seven arrows, and with each arrow killed a man of their nobles. Then he said: 'O Allah, I have protected Your religion at the beginning of the day, so protect my flesh at the end of the day.' Then they surrounded him and killed him, and they wished to cut off his head to sell it to Sulafa bint Sa'd, who had killed some of her people. She vowed: 'If I get hold of his head, I will drink wine from its skull.' Allah sent a swarm of al-Dubur, which are wasps, and they shielded him so that they could not reach him. He said: 'Leave him until evening, when it will leave him, and we will take him.' A cloud came and poured down like heavy torrents, and Allah sent the valley, which carried him away and took him. They captured Khubayb and Zayd. The sons of al-Harith ibn Amir bought Khubayb in order to kill him, because he had killed their fathers. When they brought him out to kill him, he said: 'Let me pray two rak'ahs.' They left him, and he prayed two rak'ahs, then said: 'Were it not that you would say that Khubayb panicked, I would have prolonged them.' Then he recited:

I do not care, when I am killed as a Muslim, on which side I fall for the sake of Allah,
And that is for the sake of the Deity; if He wills, He will bless the scattered limbs of a torn body.

They crucified him alive. He said: 'O Allah, You know that there is no one here near me who will convey my greeting to Your Messenger.' A man among them called Abu Sirwa came with a spear and placed it between Khubayb's hands. Khubayb said to him: 'Fear Allah!' That only increased him in insolence. As for Zayd, Safwan ibn Umayya bought him to kill him in revenge for his father. Abu Sufyan ibn Harb came to him when he was brought out to be killed and said: 'O Zayd! I beseech you by Allah: would you like Muhammad to be in your place, and you to be with your family?' He said: 'By Allah, I would not like Muhammad now to be in the place where he is, where a thorn pricks him and hurts him, while I sit with my family.' Then he was killed. The news reached the Prophet ﷺ, who said: 'Which of you will take Khubayb down from his cross, and he will have Paradise?' al-Zubayr said: 'I and my companion al-Miqdad.' They set out walking by night and hiding by day, until they reached the place. Around the cross were forty polytheists, asleep and intoxicated, and Khubayb was fresh and moving, and nothing had changed in him after forty days. Al-Zubayr carried him on his horse and set off, and seventy of them caught up with him. Al-Zubayr threw Khubayb down, and the earth swallowed him. Al-Zubayr said: 'What has emboldened you against us, O company of Quraysh?' Then he removed the turban from his head and said: 'I am al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, my mother is Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib, and my companion is al-Miqdad: two lions crouching, defending their cubs. If you wish, I will shoot at you; if you wish, I will fight you face to face; and if you wish, you may withdraw.' So they withdrew. The two came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Gabriel was with him. He said: 'O Muhammad, the angels boast of these two of your companions.'

Some of the hypocrites said concerning the companions of Khubayb: 'Woe to these slain men! They neither stayed in their homes, nor delivered the message of their companion.' So Allah revealed concerning al-Zubayr, al-Miqdad, Khubayb and his companions, and the hypocrites, this verse and the three verses after it." This hadith in its entirety is narrated from Ibn Abbas.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾. There are two views on this. The first is that he says: "Allah witnesses that what my tongue utters is what is in my heart." The second is that he says: "O Allah, bear witness against me to this statement." Ibn Mas'ud read "wayastashhidu Allah" (and he calls Allah to bear witness), with the addition of a sin and a ta'. al-Hasan, Talha ibn Musarrif, Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Abla read "wayashhadu" with a fatha on the ya' and "Allahu" in the nominative (raf'), so that Allah is the subject.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And he is the most contentious of adversaries﴾. Al-khisam is the plural of khasm (adversary), and it is said: khasm, khisam, khusum. Al-Zajjaj said: al-aladd is one who is intensely contentious. Its derivation is from the two ladidayn of the neck, which are the two sides of the neck. Its meaning is that whichever way his opponent takes from the doors of dispute, he overcomes him in it.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 205:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When he turns away﴾ has four interpretations. The first is that it means "became angry," related from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Jurayj. The second is that it means turning away from the speech he had made, said by al-Hasan. The third is that it derives from *al-wilayah* (authority, rule), so that its meaning is "when he becomes a ruler," said by Mujahid and al-Dahhak. The fourth is that it means departing physically, said by Muqatil and Ibn Qutaybah.

Regarding the meaning of "strives" (*sa'a*), there are two views. The first is that it means "acts" or "works," said by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid. The second is that it derives from striving on foot, said by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

Regarding "corruption" (*fasad*), there are two views. The first is that it is disbelief (*kufr*). The second is wrongdoing (*zulm*). "Tilth" (*harth*) is crops, and "offspring" (*nasl*) is the offspring of every living creature. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah, among others. Al-Zajjaj related from some people that *harth* means women and *nasl* means children. He said: "This is not objectionable, for a woman is called *harth*."

Regarding the meaning of his destroying the crops and offspring, there are three views. The first is that it is the destruction of these through killing, burning and corruption, said by most scholars. The second is that when he does wrong, the wrong becomes a cause for the cutting off of rain, so the crops and offspring perish. This is said by Mujahid, and it fits the view of those who said the word derives from "turning away." The third is that it is the destruction of these through misguidance, which leads to ruin, related by some commentators.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And God does not love corruption﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He does not approve of sins. The Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school) have used this verse as evidence, and our companions have answered with several replies. Among them: He does not love it as a religious matter, nor does He will it as a legal matter; but as for His not willing it in existence, that is not the case. The second: He does not love it for believers while not loving it for disbelievers. The third: willing (*iradah*) is a meaning distinct from loving (*mahabbah*). A person may take bitter medicine and desire the cutting of a wound without loving either of these. When the difference between willing and loving is clear to reason, their claim of equality between the two is refuted, and this is a well-founded reply. Among the meanings of this verse is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and He does not approve disbelief for His servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 7].

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 206:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Pride took hold of him﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is al-ḥamiyyah (zealous arrogance, fierce partisan pride). And they recited:

"Pride took hold of him through his ignorance, so he turned away in anger, acting like one who is vexed."

The meaning of the speech is: zealous arrogance drove him to act sinfully. Regarding "Jahannam" there are two opinions, which Ibn al-Anbari mentioned. The first: it is a non-Arabic word, not declined (diptote) due to definiteness and foreignness. The second: it is an Arabic noun, and it was not declined due to femininity and definiteness. Ru'bah said: "a well of Jihnam: its bottom is far away."

And al-Aʿshā said:

"I called my two friends, Musahhal, and they called for him: Jihnam, a cutting-off for the disgraced, blemished hybrid."

Leaving it undeclined indicates that it is a non-Arabic word that has been Arabicized.

Regarding the meaning of the speech there are two opinions. The first: "Jahannam is sufficient for him as recompense for his sin." The second: "Jahannam is sufficient for him as humiliation in place of the pride." Al-mihad means the bedding, and "mahhadtu li-fulan" means: when I prepared a resting place for him; and from it comes "mahd al-ṣabiyy" (the cradle of the child).

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 207:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the approval of Allah﴾. The scholars differed concerning who this verse was revealed about, into five opinions.

The first: that it was revealed concerning enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil, and this is the meaning of the statement of Qamar and ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with them both. The second: that it was revealed concerning al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad when they went to take Khubayb down from his wooden post, and we have explained the story. This is the statement of Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak. The third: that it was revealed concerning Suhayb al-Rumi, and they differed about his story. It is narrated that "he set out as a migrant toward the Prophet, ﷺ, and a group of Quraysh followed him. He dismounted, emptied his quiver, and said: 'You know that I am among the best of you with the arrow, and by Allah, you will not reach me until I have shot you with every arrow I have, then I will strike you with my sword as long as there remains anything in my hand. If you wish, I will show you where my wealth is.' They said: 'Show us where your wealth is and we will leave you alone.' So he made a covenant with them on that, and this verse was revealed concerning him. When the Prophet ﷺ saw him he said: 'The sale has profited, Abu Yahya!' and he recited the Qur'an to him." This is the statement of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, and Abu Salih related something similar from Ibn ʿAbbas, and said: "The one you meet, give him the glad tidings of what was revealed concerning him; Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said it." Muqatil mentioned that he said to the polytheists: "I am an old man; it will not harm you whether I am with you or against you, and I have a right over you due to my neighbourhood. Take my wealth apart from my mount, and leave me and my religion." He stipulated that he not be prevented from prayer or from migration. So he remained as long as Allah willed, then he mounted his mount and came to Medina as a migrant. Abu Bakr met him, gave him the glad tidings, and said: "This verse was revealed concerning you." ʿIkrimah said: "It was revealed concerning Suhayb and Abu Dharr al-Ghifari. As for Suhayb, his family seized him, and he ransomed himself with his wealth. As for Abu Dharr, his family seized him, but he escaped from them until he arrived as a migrant." The fourth: that it was revealed concerning the mujahidin in the path of Allah; this was said by al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd along with others. The fifth: that it was revealed concerning the Emigrants and the Helpers when they fought for the religion of Allah until they prevailed; this is the statement of Qatadah.

"Yashri" is a word of the opposites (al-adda', words having two contrary meanings), it is said: "shara," meaning "sold," and meaning "bought." So its meaning according to the one who said it was revealed concerning Suhayb is: "yashtari" (buys). According to the rest of the opinions, its meaning is: "yabiʿu" (sells).

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ادْخُلُوا في السِّلْمِ كافَّةً﴾ (O you who believe, enter into Islam completely). اخْتَلَفُوا فِيمَن نَزَلَتْ عَلى ثَلاثَةِ أقْوالٍ. أحَدُها: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ فِيمَن أسْلَمَ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ، كانُوا بَعْدَ إسْلامِهِمْ يَتَّقُونَ السَّبْتَ ولَحْمَ الجَمَلِ، وأشْياءَ يَتَّقِيها أهْلُ الكِتابِ. رَواهُ أبُو صالِحٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّانِي: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في أهْلِ الكِتابِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِالنَّبِيِّ مُحَمَّدٍ (ﷺ)، أُمِرُوا بِالدُّخُولِ في الإسْلامِ. رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا، وبِهِ قالَ الضَّحّاكُ. والثّالِثُ: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في المُسْلِمِينَ، يَأْمُرُهم بِالدُّخُولِ في شَرائِعِ الإسْلامِ كُلِّها، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ وقَتادَةُ.

وَفِي "السِّلْمِ" ثَلاثُ لُغاتٍ: كَسْرُ السِّينِ، وتَسْكِينُ اللّامِ، وبِها قَرَأ أبُو عَمْرٍو، وابْنُ عامِرٍ في "البَقَرَةِ"، وفَتَحا السِّينَ في "الأنْفالِ" وسُورَةِ "مُحَمَّدٍ". وفَتْحُ السِّينِ مَعَ تَسْكِينِ اللّامِ، وبِها قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، ونافِعٌ، والكِسائِيُّ في المَواضِعِ الثَّلاثَةِ. وفَتْحُ السِّينِ واللّامِ، وبِها قَرَأ الأعْمَشُ في "البَقَرَةِ" خاصَّةً.

(p-٢٢٥)وَفِي مَعْنى "السِّلْمِ" قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ الإسْلامُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وقَتادَةُ، والضَّحّاكُ، والسُّدِّيُّ، وابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ، والزَّجّاجُ في آخَرِينَ. والثّانِي: أنَّها الطّاعَةُ، رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا، وهو قَوْلُ أبِي العالِيَةِ، والرَّبِيعِ.

وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: و"كافَّةً" بِمَعْنى الجَمِيعِ، وهو في اشْتِقاقِ اللُّغَةِ: ما يَكُفُّ الشَّيْءَ في آخِرِهِ. مِن ذَلِكَ: كَفَّهُ القَمِيصُ، وكُلُّ مُسْتَطِيلٍ فَحَرَّفَهُ كُفَّةٌ، بِضَمِّ الكافِ. ويُقالُ: في كُلِّ مُسْتَدِيرٍ: كِفَّهُ بِكَسْرِ الكافِ، نَحْوُ: كِفَّةُ المِيزانِ. ويُقالُ: إنَّما سُمِّيَتْ كُفَّةَ الثَّوْبِ، لِأنَّها تَمْنَعُهُ أنْ يَنْتَشِرَ. وأصْلُ الكَفِّ: المَنعُ، وقِيلَ لِطَرَفِ اليَدِ: كَفٌّ، لِأنَّها تَكُفُّ بِها عَنْ سائِرِ البَدَنِ، ورَجُلٌ مَكْفُوفٌ: قَدْ كُفَّ بَصَرُهُ أنْ يَنْظُرَ.

واخْتَلَفُوا: هَلْ قَوْلُهُ "كافَّةً" يَرْجِعُ إلى السِّلْمِ، أوْ إلى الدّاخِلِينَ فِيهِ؟ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ راجِعٌ إلى السِّلْمِ، فَتَقْدِيرُهُ: ادْخُلُوا في جَمِيعِ شَرائِعِ الإسْلامِ. وهَذا يَخْرُجُ عَلى القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ الَّذِي ذَكَرْناهُ في نُزُولِ الآيَةِ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ يَرْجِعُ إلى الدّاخِلِينَ فِيهِ، فَتَقْدِيرُهُ: ادْخُلُوا كُلُّكم في الإسْلامِ. وبِهَذا يَخْرُجُ عَلى القَوْلِ الثّانِي.

وعَلى القَوْلِ الثّالِثِ يُحْتَمَلُ قَوْلُهُ "كافَّةً" ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ. أحَدُها: أنْ يَكُونَ أمْرًا لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِألْسِنَتِهِمْ أنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِقُلُوبِهِمْ. والثّانِي: أنْ يَكُونَ أمْرًا لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِالدُّخُولِ في جَمِيعِ شَرائِعِهِ. والثّالِثُ: أنْ يَكُونَ أمْرًا لَهم بِالثَّباتِ عَلَيْهِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا﴾ (O you who believe, believe) [النِّساءِ: ١٣٦]. و"خُطُواتُ الشَّيْطانِ" المَعاصِي، وقَدْ سَبَقَ شَرْحُها. و"البَيِّناتُ" الدَّلالاتُ الواضِحاتُ. وقالَ ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ: هي الإسْلامُ والقُرْآنُ. و"يَنْظُرُونَ" بِمَعْنى: يَنْتَظِرُونَ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إلا أنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ (unless God comes to them). كانَ جَماعَةٌ مِنَ السَّلَفِ (the early generations) يُمْسِكُونَ عَنِ الكَلامِ في مِثْلِ هَذا. وقَدْ ذَكَرَ القاضِي أبُو يَعْلى عَنْ أحْمَدَ أنَّهُ قالَ: المُرادُ بِهِ: قُدْرَتُهُ وأمْرُهُ. قالَ: وقَدْ بَيَّنَهُ في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿أوْ يَأْتِيَ أمْرُ رَبِّكَ﴾ (or the command of your Lord comes) [الأنْعامِ: ١٥٨].

(p-٢٢٦)قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فِي ظُلَلٍ مِنَ الغَمامِ﴾ (in canopies of clouds) أيْ: بِظُلَلٍ. والظُّلَلُ: جَمْعُ ظُلَّةٍ. و"الغَمامُ": السَّحابُ الَّذِي لا ماءَ فِيهِ. قالَ الضَّحّاكُ: في قِطَعٍ مِنَ السَّحابِ. ومَتى يَكُونُ مَجِيءُ المَلائِكَةِ؟ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ يَوْمُ القِيامَةِ، وهو قَوْلُ الجُمْهُورِ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ عِنْدَ المَوْتِ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. وقَرَأ الحَسَنُ بِخَفْضِ "المَلائِكَةِ". و﴿قُضِيَ الأمْرُ﴾ (the matter is decided): فَرَغَ مِنهُ. ﴿وَإلى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ﴾ (and to God all matters are returned): أيْ: تَصِيرُ. قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ ونافِعٌ وأبُو عَمْرٍو وعاصِمٌ "تُرْجَعُ" بِضَمِّ التّاءِ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ عامِرٍ، وحَمْزَةُ، والكِسائِيُّ بِفَتْحِها.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: فَكَأنَّ الأُمُورَ كانَتْ إلى غَيْرِهِ؟ فَعَنْهُ أرْبَعَةُ أجْوِبَةٍ. أحَدُها: أنَّ المُرادَ بِهِ إعْلامُ الخَلْقِ أنَّهُ المُجازِي عَلى الأعْمالِ بِالثَّوابِ والعِقابِ، قالَهُ الزَّجّاجُ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ لَمّا عَبَدَ قَوْمٌ غَيْرَهُ، ونَسَبُوا أفْعالَهُ إلى سِواهُ، ثُمَّ انْكَشَفَ الغِطاءُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ؛ رَدُّوا إلَيْهِ ما أضافُوهُ إلى غَيْرِهِ. والثّالِثُ: أنَّ العَرَبَ تَقُولُ: قَدْ رَجَعَ عَلَيَّ مِن فُلانٍ مَكْرُوهٌ، إذا صارَ إلَيْهِ مِنهُ مَكْرُوهٌ، وإنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ سَبَقَ، قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

فَإنْ تَكُنِ الأيّامُ أحْسَنَ مَرَّةً ... إلَيَّ فَقَدْ عادَتْ لَهُنَّ ذُنُوبُ

(If days were once kind to me, their wrongs have since returned to them.)

ذَكَرَهُما ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ. ومِمّا يُشْبِهُ هَذا قَوْلُ لَبِيدٍ:

وما المَرْءُ إلّا كالشِّهابِ وضَوْئِهِ ... يَحُورُ رَمادًا بَعْدَ إذْ هو ساطِعُ

(A man is but like a meteor and its light: it turns to ashes after it was blazing.)

أرادَ: يَصِيرُ رَمادًا، لا أنَّهُ كانَ رَمادًا. وقالَ أُمَيَّةُ بْنُ أبِي الصَّلْتِ:

تِلْكَ المَكارِمُ لا قِعْبانَ مِن لَبَنٍ ... شَيَّبا بِماءٍ فَعادا بَعْدَ أبْوالًا

(Those are noble deeds, not two bowls of milk mixed with water that then turned into urine.)

أيْ: صارَ. والرّابِعُ: أنَّهُ لَمّا كانَتِ الأُمُورُ إلَيْهِ قَبْلَ الخَلْقِ، ثُمَّ أوْجَدَهُمْ فَمَلَّكَهُمْ بَعْضَها، رَجَعَتْ إلَيْهِ بَعْدَ هَلاكِهِمْ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: قَدْ جَرى ذِكْرُ اسْمِهِ تَعالى في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ فَما (p-٢٢٧) الحِكْمَةُ في أنَّهُ لَمْ يَقُلْ: وإلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ؟ فالجَوابُ: أنَّ إعادَةَ اسْمِهِ أفْخَمُ وأعْظَمُ، والعَرَبُ إذا جَرى ذِكْرُ شَيْءٍ يُفَخَّمُ أعادُوا لَفْظَهُ، وأنْشَدُوا:

لا أرى المَوْتَ يَسْبِقُ المَوْتَ شَيْئًا ... نَغَّصَ المَوْتُ ذا الغِنى والفَقِيرا

(I see no thing outpacing death; death has embittered both the rich man and the poor.)

فَأعادُوا ذِكْرَ المَوْتِ لِفَخامَتِهِ في صُدُورِهِمْ، ذَكَرَهُ الزَّجّاجُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ادْخُلُوا في السِّلْمِ كافَّةً﴾ (O you who believe, enter into Islam completely). اخْتَلَفُوا فِيمَن نَزَلَتْ عَلى ثَلاثَةِ أقْوالٍ. أحَدُها: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ فِيمَن أسْلَمَ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ، كانُوا بَعْدَ إسْلامِهِمْ يَتَّقُونَ السَّبْتَ ولَحْمَ الجَمَلِ، وأشْياءَ يَتَّقِيها أهْلُ الكِتابِ. رَواهُ أبُو صالِحٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّانِي: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في أهْلِ الكِتابِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِالنَّبِيِّ مُحَمَّدٍ (ﷺ)، أُمِرُوا بِالدُّخُولِ في الإسْلامِ. رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا، وبِهِ قالَ الضَّحّاكُ. والثّالِثُ: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في المُسْلِمِينَ، يَأْمُرُهم بِالدُّخُولِ في شَرائِعِ الإسْلامِ كُلِّها، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ وقَتادَةُ.

وَفِي "السِّلْمِ" ثَلاثُ لُغاتٍ: كَسْرُ السِّينِ، وتَسْكِينُ اللّامِ، وبِها قَرَأ أبُو عَمْرٍو، وابْنُ عامِرٍ في "البَقَرَةِ"، وفَتَحا السِّينَ في "الأنْفالِ" وسُورَةِ "مُحَمَّدٍ". وفَتْحُ السِّينِ مَعَ تَسْكِينِ اللّامِ، وبِها قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، ونافِعٌ، والكِسائِيُّ في المَواضِعِ الثَّلاثَةِ. وفَتْحُ السِّينِ واللّامِ، وبِها قَرَأ الأعْمَشُ في "البَقَرَةِ" خاصَّةً.

واخْتَلَفُوا: هَلْ قَوْلُهُ "كافَّةً" يَرْجِعُ إلى السِّلْمِ، أوْ إلى الدّاخِلِينَ فِيهِ؟ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ راجِعٌ إلى السِّلْمِ، فَتَقْدِيرُهُ: ادْخُلُوا في جَمِيعِ شَرائِعِ الإسْلامِ. وهَذا يَخْرُجُ عَلى القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ الَّذِي ذَكَرْناهُ في نُزُولِ الآيَةِ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ يَرْجِعُ إلى الدّاخِلِينَ فِيهِ، فَتَقْدِيرُهُ: ادْخُلُوا كُلُّكم في الإسْلامِ. وبِهَذا يَخْرُجُ عَلى القَوْلِ الثّانِي.

(I see no thing outpacing death; death has embittered both the rich man and the poor.)

فَأعادُوا ذِكْرَ المَوْتِ لِفَخامَتِهِ في صُدُورِهِمْ، ذَكَرَهُ الزَّجّاجُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ادْخُلُوا في السِّلْمِ كافَّةً﴾ (O you who believe, enter into Islam completely). اخْتَلَفُوا فِيمَن نَزَلَتْ عَلى ثَلاثَةِ أقْوالٍ. أحَدُها: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ فِيمَن أسْلَمَ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ، كانُوا بَعْدَ إسْلامِهِمْ يَتَّقُونَ السَّبْتَ ولَحْمَ الجَمَلِ، وأشْياءَ يَتَّقِيها أهْلُ الكِتابِ. رَواهُ أبُو صالِحٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّانِي: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في أهْلِ الكِتابِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِالنَّبِيِّ مُحَمَّدٍ (ﷺ)، أُمِرُوا بِالدُّخُولِ في الإسْلامِ. رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا، وبِهِ قالَ الضَّحّاكُ. والثّالِثُ: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ في المُسْلِمِينَ، يَأْمُرُهم بِالدُّخُولِ في شَرائِعِ الإسْلامِ كُلِّها، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ وقَتادَةُ.

وَفِي "السِّلْمِ" ثَلاثُ لُغاتٍ: كَسْرُ السِّينِ، وتَسْكِينُ اللّامِ، وبِها قَرَأ أبُو عَمْرٍو، وابْنُ عامِرٍ في "البَقَرَةِ"، وفَتَحا السِّينَ في "الأنْفالِ" وسُورَةِ "مُحَمَّدٍ". وفَتْحُ السِّينِ مَعَ تَسْكِينِ اللّامِ، وبِها قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، ونافِعٌ، والكِسائِيُّ في المَواضِعِ الثَّلاثَةِ. وفَتْحُ السِّينِ واللّامِ، وبِها قَرَأ الأعْمَشُ في "البَقَرَةِ" خاصَّةً.

(p-٢٢٥)وَفِي مَعْنى "السِّلْمِ" قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ الإسْلامُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وقَتادَةُ، والضَّحّاكُ، والسُّدِّيُّ، وابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ، والزَّجّاجُ في آخَرِينَ. والثّانِي: أنَّها الطّاعَةُ، رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا، وهو قَوْلُ أبِي العالِيَةِ، والرَّبِيعِ.

وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: و"كافَّةً" بِمَعْنى الجَمِيعِ، وهو في اشْتِقاقِ اللُّغَةِ: ما يَكُفُّ الشَّيْءَ في آخِرِهِ. مِن ذَلِكَ: كَفَّهُ القَمِيصُ، وكُلُّ مُسْتَطِيلٍ فَحَرَّفَهُ كُفَّةٌ، بِضَمِّ الكافِ. ويُقالُ: في كُلِّ مُسْتَدِيرٍ: كِفَّهُ بِكَسْرِ الكافِ، نَحْوُ: كِفَّةُ المِيزانِ. ويُقالُ: إنَّما سُمِّيَتْ كُفَّةَ الثَّوْبِ، لِأنَّها تَمْنَعُهُ أنْ يَنْتَشِرَ. وأصْلُ الكَفِّ: المَنعُ، وقِيلَ لِطَرَفِ اليَدِ: كَفٌّ، لِأنَّها تَكُفُّ بِها عَنْ سائِرِ البَدَنِ، ورَجُلٌ مَكْفُوفٌ: قَدْ كُفَّ بَصَرُهُ أنْ يَنْظُرَ.

واخْتَلَفُوا: هَلْ قَوْلُهُ "كافَّةً" يَرْجِعُ إلى السِّلْمِ، أوْ إلى الدّاخِلِينَ فِيهِ؟ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ راجِعٌ إلى السِّلْمِ، فَتَقْدِيرُهُ: ادْخُلُوا في جَمِيعِ شَرائِعِ الإسْلامِ. وهَذا يَخْرُجُ عَلى القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ الَّذِي ذَكَرْناهُ في نُزُولِ الآيَةِ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ يَرْجِعُ إلى الدّاخِلِينَ فِيهِ، فَتَقْدِيرُهُ: ادْخُلُوا كُلُّكم في الإسْلامِ. وبِهَذا يَخْرُجُ عَلى القَوْلِ الثّانِي.

وعَلى القَوْلِ الثّالِثِ يُحْتَمَلُ قَوْلُهُ "كافَّةً" ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ. أحَدُها: أنْ يَكُونَ أمْرًا لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِألْسِنَتِهِمْ أنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِقُلُوبِهِمْ. والثّانِي: أنْ يَكُونَ أمْرًا لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِالدُّخُولِ في جَمِيعِ شَرائِعِهِ. والثّالِثُ: أنْ يَكُونَ أمْرًا لَهم بِالثَّباتِ عَلَيْهِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا﴾ (O you who believe, believe) [النِّساءِ: ١٣٦]. و"خُطُواتُ الشَّيْطانِ" المَعاصِي، وقَدْ سَبَقَ شَرْحُها. و"البَيِّناتُ" الدَّلالاتُ الواضِحاتُ. وقالَ ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ: هي الإسْلامُ والقُرْآنُ. و"يَنْظُرُونَ" بِمَعْنى: يَنْتَظِرُونَ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إلا أنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ (unless God comes to them). كانَ جَماعَةٌ مِنَ السَّلَفِ (the early generations) يُمْسِكُونَ عَنِ الكَلامِ في مِثْلِ هَذا. وقَدْ ذَكَرَ القاضِي أبُو يَعْلى عَنْ أحْمَدَ أنَّهُ قالَ: المُرادُ بِهِ: قُدْرَتُهُ وأمْرُهُ. قالَ: وقَدْ بَيَّنَهُ في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿أوْ يَأْتِيَ أمْرُ رَبِّكَ﴾ (or the command of your Lord comes) [الأنْعامِ: ١٥٨].

(p-٢٢٦)قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فِي ظُلَلٍ مِنَ الغَمامِ﴾ (in canopies of clouds) أيْ: بِظُلَلٍ. والظُّلَلُ: جَمْعُ ظُلَّةٍ. و"الغَمامُ": السَّحابُ الَّذِي لا ماءَ فِيهِ. قالَ الضَّحّاكُ: في قِطَعٍ مِنَ السَّحابِ. ومَتى يَكُونُ مَجِيءُ المَلائِكَةِ؟ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ يَوْمُ القِيامَةِ، وهو قَوْلُ الجُمْهُورِ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ عِنْدَ المَوْتِ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. وقَرَأ الحَسَنُ بِخَفْضِ "المَلائِكَةِ". و﴿قُضِيَ الأمْرُ﴾ (the matter is decided): فَرَغَ مِنهُ. ﴿وَإلى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ﴾ (and to God all matters are returned): أيْ: تَصِيرُ. قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ ونافِعٌ وأبُو عَمْرٍو وعاصِمٌ "تُرْجَعُ" بِضَمِّ التّاءِ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ عامِرٍ، وحَمْزَةُ، والكِسائِيُّ بِفَتْحِها.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: فَكَأنَّ الأُمُورَ كانَتْ إلى غَيْرِهِ؟ فَعَنْهُ أرْبَعَةُ أجْوِبَةٍ. أحَدُها: أنَّ المُرادَ بِهِ إعْلامُ الخَلْقِ أنَّهُ المُجازِي عَلى الأعْمالِ بِالثَّوابِ والعِقابِ، قالَهُ الزَّجّاجُ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ لَمّا عَبَدَ قَوْمٌ غَيْرَهُ، ونَسَبُوا أفْعالَهُ إلى سِواهُ، ثُمَّ انْكَشَفَ الغِطاءُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ؛ رَدُّوا إلَيْهِ ما أضافُوهُ إلى غَيْرِهِ. والثّالِثُ: أنَّ العَرَبَ تَقُولُ: قَدْ رَجَعَ عَلَيَّ مِن فُلانٍ مَكْرُوهٌ، إذا صارَ إلَيْهِ مِنهُ مَكْرُوهٌ، وإنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ سَبَقَ، قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

فَإنْ تَكُنِ الأيّامُ أحْسَنَ مَرَّةً ... إلَيَّ فَقَدْ عادَتْ لَهُنَّ ذُنُوبُ

(If days were once kind to me, their wrongs have since returned to them.)

ذَكَرَهُما ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ. ومِمّا يُشْبِهُ هَذا قَوْلُ لَبِيدٍ:

وما المَرْءُ إلّا كالشِّهابِ وضَوْئِهِ ... يَحُورُ رَمادًا بَعْدَ إذْ هو ساطِعُ

(A man is but like a meteor and its light: it turns to ashes after it was blazing.)

أرادَ: يَصِيرُ رَمادًا، لا أنَّهُ كانَ رَمادًا. وقالَ أُمَيَّةُ بْنُ أبِي الصَّلْتِ:

تِلْكَ المَكارِمُ لا قِعْبانَ مِن لَبَنٍ ... شَيَّبا بِماءٍ فَعادا بَعْدَ أبْوالًا

(Those are noble deeds, not two bowls of milk mixed with water that then turned into urine.)

أيْ: صارَ. والرّابِعُ: أنَّهُ لَمّا كانَتِ الأُمُورُ إلَيْهِ قَبْلَ الخَلْقِ، ثُمَّ أوْجَدَهُمْ فَمَلَّكَهُمْ بَعْضَها، رَجَعَتْ إلَيْهِ بَعْدَ هَلاكِهِمْ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: قَدْ جَرى ذِكْرُ اسْمِهِ تَعالى في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ فَما (p-٢٢٧) الحِكْمَةُ في أنَّهُ لَمْ يَقُلْ: وإلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ؟ فالجَوابُ: أنَّ إعادَةَ اسْمِهِ أفْخَمُ وأعْظَمُ، والعَرَبُ إذا جَرى ذِكْرُ شَيْءٍ يُفَخَّمُ أعادُوا لَفْظَهُ، وأنْشَدُوا:

لا أرى المَوْتَ يَسْبِقُ المَوْتَ شَيْئًا ... نَغَّصَ المَوْتُ ذا الغِنى والفَقِيرا

(I see no thing outpacing death; death has embittered both the rich man and the poor.)

فَأعادُوا ذِكْرَ المَوْتِ لِفَخامَتِهِ في صُدُورِهِمْ، ذَكَرَهُ الزَّجّاجُ.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 211:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Ask the Children of Israel﴾ The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the meaning includes him and the believers. Al-Farra' said: The people of the Hijaz say "sal" without a hamza, some of Tamim say "is'al" with a hamza, and some of them say "isal" with an alif and the dropping of the hamza. The first of these is the most unusual of them, and the Book came with it. There are two views regarding the intended meaning of the asking. One: it is confirmation and reminder of the blessings. The second: it is a rebuke for neglecting gratitude.

The clear sign (al-ayah al-bayyinah) is the manifest proof, such as the staff, the cloud, the manna, the quails, and the sea. There are two views regarding the meaning of the blessing of Allah. One: it is the signs we have mentioned, as said by Qatadah. The second: it is the proofs of Allah indicating the affair of the Prophet (ﷺ), as said by al-Zajjaj.

Regarding the meaning of changing them (tabdiluha) there are three views. The first: that it is disbelief in them, as said by Abu al-'Aliyah and Mujahid. The second: altering the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Torah, as said by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi. The third: nullifying the proofs of Allah through corrupt interpretations.

(p-228) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The worldly life is made attractive to those who disbelieve﴾. Regarding its revelation there are three opinions. The first: it was revealed about Abu Jahl and his companions; this is related from Ibn Abbas. The second: it was revealed about the scholars of the Jews; this is related from Ata'. The third: it was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions from among the hypocrites; this is related from Muqatil. Al-Zajjaj said: The masculine form was permitted in "zuyyina" (was made attractive) because the feminine of "al-hayah" (life) is not a true feminine, since the meaning of "al-hayah" and the meaning of "al-'aysh" (livelihood) are one and the same.

As for the one to whom this making-attractive is attributed, there are two opinions. The first: it is attributed to Allah. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "zayyana" with a fathah on the zay and the ya, meaning: Allah made it attractive to them. The second: it is attributed to Satan; this is narrated from al-Hasan. Our shaykh Ali ibn Ubayd Allah said: The making-attractive from Allah Exalted is the natural composition, for He placed in natures the love of what is loved, for a form in it that is adorned to the self; and that is from His workmanship. The making-attractive by Satan is by reminding (of what has occurred) of heedlessness regarding that which, like it, calls to itself by its adornment. So Allah Exalted makes attractive by placement, and Satan makes attractive by reminding.

What is the reason for the disbelievers' mockery of the believers? There are three opinions regarding this. The first: they mocked them for their poverty. The second: because of their affirmation of the Hereafter. The third: because of their following the Prophet (ﷺ). It was said: They used to make them imagine that you are upon the truth, as a mockery of them.

Regarding the meaning of their being ﴿above them﴾ there are three opinions. The first: that this is on its literal basis, because the believers are in 'Illiyyin and the disbelievers are in Sijjin. The second: that the proofs of the believers are above the doubts of the disbelievers, so they are the victorious ones. The third: that the bliss of the believers in Paradise is above the bliss of the disbelievers in the world.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions. The first: that He provides for whom He wills (p-229) abundant provision, not restricted. The second: He provides for whom He wills without being called to account in the Hereafter.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 213:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Mankind was one community﴾. Regarding the meaning of "mankind" here, there are three opinions. The first is that it refers to all the children of Adam; this is the view of the majority. The second is that it refers to Adam alone; this was said by Mujahid. Ibn al-Anbari said: This interpretation is permissible, because the Arabs use the plural form for the singular. The meaning of the verse would then be: Adam had one religion, and his offspring differed after him. The third is that Adam and his children were upon the truth, and they differed when Qabil and Habil were killed. This was mentioned by Ibn al-Anbari. The word "ummah" (community) here means a category, or a single group upon one purpose.

Regarding that purpose upon which they were, there are two opinions. One is that it was Islam; this was said by Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Muqatil. The other is that it was disbelief; this was narrated by Ata' from Ibn Abbas.

As for when that was, there are five opinions. The first is that it was when they were presented to Adam and acknowledged servitude; this was said by Ubayy ibn Ka'b. The second is that in the time of Ibrahim they were disbelievers; this was said by Ibn Abbas. The third is that it was between Adam and Nuh; this is the view of Qatadah. The fourth is that when they boarded the ark, they were upon the truth; this was said by Muqatil. The fifth is that it was in the time of Adam; this was mentioned by Ibn al-Anbari.

﴿So Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news﴾ of Paradise, ﴿and warners﴾ of the Fire. This is the view of the majority. Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: as bringers of good news to whoever believes in you, O Muhammad (ﷺ), and as warners to whoever denies you.

﴿And He sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between the people﴾. "Al-Kitab" (the Book) is a generic noun, just as you say: "The dirham has become abundant in the hands of the people." Some of them mentioned that it refers to the Torah.

Regarding the meaning of "truth" here, there are two opinions. One is that it means truthfulness and justice. The other is that it means judgment concerning what they differed about.

﴿to judge between the people﴾: regarding the judge here, there are three opinions. The first is that it is Allah, exalted is He. The second is that it is the prophet to whom the Book was revealed. The third is that it is the Book, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This Book of Ours speaks against you with truth﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29]. Abu Ja'far recited "liyahkuma" with a dammah on the yaa' and a fathah on the kaaf (i.e., the verb with the subject being Allah or the Book). Mujahid recited "litahkuma" with the taa', addressing the Prophet (ﷺ).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿concerning that in which they differed﴾: meaning, the religion.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And none differed over it﴾. Regarding this pronoun (the hā'), there are three opinions. The first is that it refers to Muhammad (ﷺ); this was said by Ibn Mas'ud. The second is that it refers to the religion; this was said by Muqatil. The third is that it refers to the Book; this was said by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi. As for the hā' in "utuhu" (they were given it), it refers to the Book without any difference of opinion. Al-Zajjaj said: "Baghyan" (out of envy) is put in the accusative as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu). The meaning is: they did not cause the difference except out of envy, because they knew the reality of the matter from their own books. Al-Farra' said: Regarding their difference there are two aspects. One is that some of them disbelieved in the Book of others. The other is that they altered what they had altered.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed﴾: that is, to knowing what they differed about, or to correcting what they differed about.

Regarding that over which they differed, there are six opinions. The first is that it is Friday. The Jews made it Saturday, and the Christians made it Sunday. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated in their Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "We are the last (in time) but the first (in precedence) on the Day of Resurrection, although they were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them. This is their day which was enjoined upon them, but they differed concerning it, so Allah guided us to it. So today is ours, tomorrow is for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow is for the Christians." The second is that it is the prayer; some of them pray facing the east, and some of them pray facing the west. The third is that it is Ibrahim: the Jews said he was a Jew, and the Christians said he was a Christian. The fourth is that it is Isa (Jesus): the Jews made him (the subject of) a slander, and the Christians made him a god. The fifth is that it is the Books: they believed in some of them and disbelieved in some of them. The sixth is that it is the religion, and this is the most correct view, because all the other opinions are included in it.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿by His permission﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: His permission (idhnihi) means His knowledge. Others said: His command. Some of them said: His enabling success (tawfiq).

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 214:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or did you suppose that you would enter Paradise﴾. Regarding the occasion of its revelation, there are three reports. The first: the Companions were afflicted on the Day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab) with calamity and siege, so this verse was revealed. This was related by al-Suddi from his teachers, and it is the view of Qatada. The second: when the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions entered Madina, harm befell them severely, so this verse was revealed. This was stated by Ata'. The third: the hypocrites said to the believers, "If Muhammad were a prophet, he would not have let you be killed." They replied, "Whoever among us is killed enters Paradise." They said, "Why do you deceive yourselves with falsehood?" Then this verse was revealed (p-232). This was stated by Muqatil, who claimed that it was revealed on the Day of Uhud.

Al-Farra' said: ﴿Did you suppose﴾ means "did you think." Al-Zajjaj said: "Am" (أمْ) means "rather" (بَلْ). We have explained "am" in what preceded with a sufficient explanation. "Al-mathal" (المَثَلُ) means "the attribute" or "the description." "Zulzilu" (زُلْزِلُوا) means they were frightened and shaken with that which causes harm. The root of "zalzala" (الزَّلْزَلَةُ) in the language is from "zalla al-shay'u 'an makanihi" (the thing slipped from its place). When you say "zalzaltuhu," its meaning is that you repeated the slipping of it from its place. Everything in which there is oscillation has the first radical of the verb repeated in it. You say "aqalla fulan al-shay'" (someone lifted the thing) when he raises it from its place; when he repeatedly lifts it and returns it, it is said "qalqalahu" (he repeatedly shook it). So the meaning is that the shaking by fear was repeated upon them, as Ibn Abbas stated. "Al-ba'sa'" (البَأْساءُ) means hardship and distress, and "al-darra'" (الضَّرّاءُ) means calamity and illness. Every messenger who was sent to his community would say: ﴿When will the help of Allah come?﴾ "Al-nasr" (النَّصْرُ) means victory. The majority read "hatta yaqula" (حَتّى يَقُولَ) with a fatha on the lam, while Nafi' read it with a damma.

**Section (fasl)**

The meaning of the verse is that the calamity and hardship reached the earlier nations to the point that they grew impatient for victory because of the severity of the trial. It indicates that the path to Paradise is only through patience upon trials. 'A'isha said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not eat his fill of wheat bread for three consecutive days until he departed to his Lord." Hudhayfa said: "The most pleasing of my days to my eyes is the day I return to my family and they complain to me of need." It was said: "And why is that?" He said: "Because I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Allah tests the believer with trials just as a parent cares for his child [with good], and Allah protects the believer from this world just as a sick person protects his family from food.'"

Abu Bakr al-Sufi informed us, saying: Abu Sa'id ibn Abi Sadiq informed us, saying: Abu Abd Allah al-Shirazi informed us, saying: I heard Abu al-Tayyib ibn al-Farkhan say: I heard al-Junayd say: I entered upon Sirri al-Saqati while he was saying (p-233):

"I did not desire to enter upon Him until I descended to His station, the lowly servant."

"I closed my eyelids over its specks, and I guarded my soul from 'he said' and 'it was said.'"

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 215:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They ask you what they should spend﴾. Concerning the occasion of its revelation there are two accounts. The first: "It was revealed concerning ʿAmr ibn al-Jamuh al-Ansari, who had much wealth, and he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, with what should we give charity, and upon whom should we spend?' So this verse was revealed." This was related by Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas. The second: "A man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'I have one dinar.' He said: 'Spend it on yourself.' He said: 'I have two dinars.' He said: 'Spend them on your family.' He said: 'I have three.' He said: 'Spend them on your servant.' He said: 'I have four.' He said: 'Spend them on your parents.' He said: 'I have five.' He said: 'Spend them on your relatives.' He said: 'I have six.' He said: 'Spend them in the way of Allah, and it is the best of them.' So this verse was revealed." This was related by ʿAta' from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Al-Zajjaj said: "Ma dha" in the language is of two kinds. The first: that "dha" is in the sense of "alladhi" (who/which), and "yunfiquna" is its relative clause, so the meaning is: "They ask you: what is that which they spend?" The second: that "ma" together with "dha" is a single noun, so the meaning is: "They ask you what thing they should spend." He said: It is as if they asked: upon whom ought they to bestow in excess, and what is the manner of what they spend? For they knew what the spender is, and Allah informed them that the most deserving of being given to are the parents and the nearest relatives. "Al-khayr" means wealth; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and others. He said: The meaning of "for the parents" (fa-lil-walidayn) is "upon the parents."

Section

Most scholars of tafsir hold that this verse is abrogated (mansukh). Ibn Masʿud said: "The verse of zakat abrogated it." Al-Hasan, however, held that it is muhkam (not abrogated). Ibn Zayd said: "It concerns voluntary charity (nawafil)." This is the apparent meaning of the verse, because its apparent sense implies recommendation (nadb), and it is not correct to say that it is abrogated, except if one says that it necessitated the obligation of maintenance (nafaqah) upon those mentioned in it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 216:

God's words: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: When God made jihad obligatory upon the Muslims, it was hard for them and they disliked it, so this verse was revealed. The word "kutiba" (was prescribed) means "furida" (was made obligatory), according to the consensus of the scholars. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said, "karihtu al-shay'a, akrahuhu, karhan and kurhan, and karaha and karahiyya." Everything in the Book of God that concerns "al-kurh" (dislike) permits the vowelling with a fatha (kark), except that Abu 'Ubayd mentioned that the people agree on pronouncing this letter, in this verse, with a damma (kurh). They disliked it only because of its hardship on the souls, not because they disliked God's obligation. Al-Farra' said: "Al-kurh" and "al-karh" are two dialects. It seems that the grammarians hold that "al-kurh" (with a damma) refers to what comes from you while you were not forced into it, but when you are forced into something, they prefer "kurhan" (with a fatha). Ibn Qutayba said: "Al-kurh" with a fatha means compulsion and coercion, and with a damma means hardship. Among the parallels to this are "al-juhd" (exertion or capacity) and "al-juhd" (hardship), though some treat them as one word. Also "'izm al-shay'" (the size of a thing) means its greatest part, and "'azamat nafsihi" (his self-importance). "'Arḍ al-shay'" means one of its sides, and "'arduhu" means its opposite of its length. "Al-akl" is the verbal noun of "akalat," and "al-akl" means the food that is eaten. Abu 'Ali said: These are two dialects, like "al-faqr" and "al-fuqr," "al-ḍa'f" and "al-ḍu'f," "al-daff" and "al-duff," and "al-shahd" and "al-shuhd."

God's words: ﴿But it may be that you dislike a thing﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: It means jihad. ﴿And it is good for you﴾: victory and booty, or martyrdom. ﴿And it may be that you love a thing﴾, which is: remaining behind from it. ﴿And it is bad for you﴾: you will gain no victory, no booty, and no martyrdom. ﴿And God knows﴾ that jihad is good for you. ﴿And you know not﴾ when you loved remaining behind from it.

Section

The scholars of al-nasikh wa'l-mansukh (abrogating and abrogated rulings) differed concerning this verse in three opinions.

The first: it is among the muhkam (clear, definitive rulings) that abrogates the pardon of the polytheists. The second: it is abrogated, because it made jihad obligatory on everyone, so that was abrogated by God's words: ﴿And the believers should not all go forth to battle﴾ (9:122). The third: it is abrogating in one respect and abrogated in another respect.

They said: The situation regarding fighting passed through three stages. The first was the prohibition of fighting, and among this is God's words: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands"?﴾ (4:77). The second: He commanded everyone to fight, and among this is God's words: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ (9:41), and this verse is similar to it. The third: fighting became a communal obligation (fard al-kifaya), and this is God's words: ﴿And the believers should not all go forth to battle﴾ (9:122). Thus what abrogates from these is the obligation of fighting after its prohibition, and what is abrogated is the obligation of fighting upon everyone.

(p-٢٣٦) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it.﴾ Jundub ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a detachment and appointed Abu ʿUbayda over them. When he set out to depart, he wept out of longing (ṣabābah) for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So he sent ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh in his place and wrote him a letter, and ordered him not to read it until he reached such-and-such a place. He said: "Do not compel any of your companions to march with you." When he reached the place, he read the letter and said the words of return (istirjaʿa), and said: "Hearing and obeying the command of Allah and His Messenger." [He then informed them of the news and read the letter to them.] Two men from among his companions turned back, and the rest went on. They came upon Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī and killed him, but they did not know on that day whether it was in Rajab or in Jumada al-Akhirah. The polytheists said to the Muslims: "You have killed in the sacred month." [They came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him the story.] Then this verse was revealed. Some of the Muslims said: "If they gained any good, they will have no reward." So there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:218]. Al-Zuhri said: The name of Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī was ʿAmr, and the name of the one who killed him was ʿAbd Allah ibn Waqid al-Laythi. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The companions of the Prophet ﷺ used to think that night was from Jumada, but it was the first of Rajab.

ʿAṭiyyah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that it was revealed concerning two matters. One of them is this. The second is (p-٢٣٧) the entry of the Prophet ﷺ into Mecca in a sacred month on the day of the Conquest, when the polytheists criticized him for fighting in a sacred month.

Regarding those who asked the Prophet ﷺ about this, there are two views. One is that they were the Muslims who asked him whether they had erred or been right. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, and Muqatil. The second is that they were the polytheists who asked him in a manner of reproach against the Muslims. This was said by al-Ḥasan, ʿUrwah, and Mujahid.

The sacred month is the month of Rajab, and it was called "the Deaf" (al-Aṣamm), because no clatter of weapons was heard in it, out of reverence for it. ﴿Fighting in it﴾ means: they ask you about fighting in it. ﴿Say: Fighting in it is great.﴾ Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is not permissible. Al-Qadi Abu Yaʿla said: The people of the Jahiliyyah believed in the prohibition of fighting in these months, so Allah, may He be exalted, informed them in this verse that the prohibition remains.

Section

The scholars differed over whether the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months remains or has been abrogated (nasakh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revealed text), on two views.

One is that it remains. Ibn Jurayj narrated that ʿAṭāʾ used to swear by Allah: "It is not permissible for people now to make a raid in the Sacred Precinct or in the sacred months, unless they are fought there or raid. And it has not been abrogated."

The second is that it has been abrogated. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar said: fighting is permissible in the sacred month, and this verse is abrogated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:5], and by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:29]. This is the view of the jurists of the cities.

(p-٢٣٨) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And hindering from the way of Allah﴾ is in the nominative case as a subject (mubtada'), and the predicate of these things is ﴿greater in the sight of Allah﴾. There are two views regarding what is meant by "the way of Allah" here.

One is that it is the Hajj, because they barred the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Mecca. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Suddi, from his shaykhs.

The second is that it is Islam. This was said by Muqatil. Regarding the pronoun in His saying ﴿and disbelief in Him﴾ there are two views. One is that it refers to Allah, may He be exalted. This was said by al-Suddi from his shaykhs, Qatadah, Muqatil, and Ibn Qutaybah. The second is that it refers to the way. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn Qutaybah said: The genitive "al-Masjid al-Haram" (the Sacred Mosque) is in coordination with His saying "the way of Allah," as if He had said: "and hindering from the way of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the expulsion of its people from it﴾. When they harmed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions, they compelled them to leave, so it was as if they had expelled them. So Allah informed them that these acts are greater than the killing of any disbeliever. "Fitnah" here means shirk (polytheism). This was said by Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and the majority. The word fitnah in the Qur'an has many meanings, which I have mentioned in the book "al-Naẓā'ir" (the Book of Parallels). ﴿And they will not cease fighting you﴾ means: the disbelievers; ﴿you﴾ means: the Muslims. And "ḥabiṭat" (has become void) means: became null.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 218:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated﴾. Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are two accounts.

The first: When the Qur'an descended with the concession to the companions of ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh concerning the killing of Ibn al-Hadrami, some of the Muslims said: "They have no reward," and so this verse was revealed. We have already mentioned this in (p-239) the occasion of revelation of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month﴾, from Jundub ibn ʿAbd Allah.

The second: When the concession was granted to them, they stood up and said: "[O Messenger of Allah,] do we hope that there will be a military campaign in which we are given the reward of the fighters?" So this verse was revealed. This was related by Ibn ʿAbbas.

He said: ﴿Emigrated﴾ means from Makkah to Madinah. ﴿And struggled﴾ in the obedience of Allah refers to Ibn al-Hadrami and his companions. And ﴿the mercy of Allah﴾ means His forgiveness and His Paradise.

Ibn al-Anbari said: In the usage of the Arabs, hijrah (emigration) means abandoning the homeland, the family and the children. The meaning of "those who emigrate" is: those who emigrate, the children and the family, so the object was known and therefore omitted.

al-Shaʿbi said: The first banner tied in Islam was the banner of ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh, and the first spoils divided in Islam were his spoils.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 2, verse 219:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling.﴾ There are two reports concerning the occasion of its revelation. The first: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said, "O Allah, make clear to us a satisfying explanation regarding wine," and then this verse was revealed. The second: "A group of the Ansar came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and among them were 'Umar and Mu'adh, and they said, 'Give us a ruling about wine, for it takes away the intellect and strips away wealth,' and then this verse was revealed."

Concerning the naming of wine as khamr (wine), there are three opinions. The first: it was called khamr because it "khamara" the intellect (khamara al-'aql), i.e., mixes with it. The second: because it covers (yukhammiru) the intellect, i.e., conceals it. The third: because it covers, i.e., conceals the mention of these sayings, Muhammad ibn al-Qasim. Al-Zajjaj said: Khamr in the linguistic sense is that which covers the intellect. It is said: "So-and-so entered the khimar of the people," meaning into the crowd, where he is hidden among them. The khimar of a woman is her veil; it was called khimar because it covers.

He said: The khamr here is that upon which there is consensus, and by analogy whatever does the same action as it should be called khamr and should have the same status in prohibition, because the scholars have unanimously agreed that all gambling is forbidden. He mentioned gambling (maysir) specifically from among them, and made all of it analogous to maysir, and maysir is only gambling in the case of the camel-carcass lottery specifically. As for maysir: Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah and others said: it is gambling. Ibn Qutaybah said: It is said "yasartu" when I struck with arrows (qidah), and the one who strikes with the arrows is called "yasir" and "yasirun," and "yusr" and "aysar."

The wealthy and generous people, in winter at the time of hardship and its severity, would slaughter a camel, divide it into portions, and then cast arrows over it. When the gambler won, he would give that to those in need and poverty, and this is the benefit which Allah mentioned. They used to boast of taking the arrows, and they would revile one another for abandoning them, and they would blame whoever did not take part in the lottery.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: In them is great sin.﴾ The majority read "kabirun" with the ba', while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the tha'.

Concerning the sin of wine there are three opinions. The first: that drinking it diminishes religion. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: that when one drinks he becomes intoxicated and harms people; this was related by al-Suddi from his shaykhs. The third: that it is the occurrence of enmity and hatred and the covering of the intellect by which discernment takes place, said by al-Zajjaj.

Concerning the sin of maysir there are two opinions. The first: that it distracts from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer, and causes enmity; this was said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: that it calls to injustice and withholding of right; this was related by al-Suddi from his shaykhs. It is permissible that all of that is intended.

As for the benefits of wine, they are of two kinds: the first is the profit in selling it; the second is the benefit to the bodies together with the enjoyment of souls. As for the benefits of maysir: a man acquires wealth without toil.

Concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And their sin is greater than their benefit.﴾ There are two opinions. The first: its meaning is: their sin after prohibition is greater than their benefit before prohibition; this was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil. The second: their sin before prohibition is greater than their benefit before prohibition too, because the sin that arises from their causes is greater than their benefit. This is also related from Ibn Jubayr. They differed on what made wine permissible, on two opinions. The first: by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And from the fruits of the date-palm and grapes you take from them intoxicant and good provision﴾ [al-Nahl: 67]; this was said by Ibn Jubayr. The second: by the earlier Shari'ah, and the Muslims acquiesced in that until it was prohibited.

Section

The scholars differed: does this verse have an effect on the prohibition of wine or not? There are two opinions. The first: that it indicates its condemnation without its prohibition; this was related by al-Suddi from his shaykhs, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah and Muqatil said so. According to this opinion, this verse is abrogated (mansukhah).

The second opinion: that it has an effect on prohibition, namely that Allah, Exalted, informed that in it is great sin, and all sin is forbidden by His saying: ﴿And sin and transgression﴾ [al-A'raf: 33]. This is the view of a group of scholars; al-Zajjaj related it, and Qadi Abu Ya'la preferred it for the reason we have explained. Some of the people of meanings argued for its soundness, saying: When Allah said, ﴿In them is great sin and benefits for people,﴾ the two matters became equal; then when He said, ﴿And their sin is greater than their benefit,﴾ sin became the predominant factor, and the benefit remained absorbed in the side of sin, so the ruling reverted to the predominant, absorbing factor, and the aspect of danger prevailed.

* Section

As for maysir, the discussion concerning it is like the discussion concerning wine. If we say that this verse indicates prohibition, then the ruling on maysir is also prohibition. If we say that it indicates reprehensibility, then the strongest opinion is that we say: the verse in al-Ma'idah explicitly states the prohibition of maysir.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they ask you what they should spend.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: The one who asked about this was 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh. Ibn Qutaybah said: What is meant by spending here is charity and giving.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: The surplus.﴾ Abu 'Amr read "al-'afw" with a raised (nominative) ending, and the rest read it with a fatha (accusative). Abu 'Ali said: "Madha" is in the accusative position, so its answer is "al-'afw" in the accusative, as you say in answer to "Madha anfaqta?" (What did you spend?): "Anfaqtu dirhaman" (I spent a dirham). This is the reason for the accusative of al-'afw. As for the one who reads it in the nominative, he makes "dha" like "alladhi" (the one which), and does not make "madha" a single word; so when someone says, "Madha anzala Rabbukum?" (What has your Lord sent down?), it is as if he said, "What is it that your Lord has sent down?" and the answer is: "Qur'an." Al-Zajjaj said: "Al-'afw" linguistically means abundance and excess; it is said: "Qad 'afa al-qawm" when the people have increased. And "al-'afw" is what comes without hardship. Ibn Qutaybah said: al-'afw is what is easy; it is said: "Take what 'afaka," i.e., what comes to you easily without compulsion or hardship.

The exegetes have five opinions about what is meant by al-'afw here.
